record.paper_title: List homomorphism problems for signed trees
record.context_brief: Irreflexive bipartite signed targets with bicoloured edges
record.original_question: For List-S-Hom(H) restricted to fixed target signed graphs H that are irreflexive, bipartite, and contain at least one bicoloured edge, and after excluding cases where the signed core already has more than two edges, which such targets H yield polynomial-time solvable signed list homomorphism problems and which yield NP-complete problems?

evidence.quote: We have observed that List-S-Hom(Hb) is NP-complete if the s-core of Hb has more than two edges. Thus we will focus on signed graphs Hb whose s-cores have at most two edges.

Thus we consider irreflexive signed graphs. The s-core is still too big if the underlying graph has an odd cycle. So in this case it remains to classify the irreflexive bipartite signed graphs that contain a bicoloured edge. Even this case is complex. We explore homomorphisms to irreflexive bipartite signed graphs in a companion paper.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A signed graph is a pair $\hat H=(H,\sigma)$ where $H=(V,E)$ is a graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+,-\}$ assigns a sign (colour) to each edge; edges with sign $+$ are called positive (one colour) and edges with sign $-$ are called negative (the other colour). A signed graph is irreflexive if it has no loops, and bipartite if its underlying graph $H$ is bipartite. An edge of $\hat H$ is unicoloured if all edges between its endpoints carry the same sign, and bicoloured if both signs occur on edges between the same pair of vertices (or, equivalently in the multigraph/switching sense used here, a pair of vertices linked by both a positive and a negative edge). 

A switching at a vertex $v$ replaces $\sigma(e)$ by $-\sigma(e)$ for every edge $e$ incident with $v$. Two signed graphs are switching-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of switchings. A homomorphism of signed graphs $f:\hat G\to\hat H$ is a homomorphism of underlying graphs from $G$ to some signed graph switching-equivalent to $\hat H$ that preserves edge signs. The s-core of $\hat H$ is the (up to switching) smallest signed subgraph $\hat H'\subseteq\hat H$ admitting a homomorphism from $\hat H$.

Problem List-S-Hom($\hat H$). Given a signed graph $\hat G$ together with lists $L(v)\subseteq V(H)$ for $v\in V(G)$, decide whether there exists a homomorphism $f:\hat G\to\hat H$ of signed graphs such that $f(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v\in V(G)$.

It is known that List-S-Hom($\hat H$) is NP-complete whenever the s-core of $\hat H$ has more than two edges.

Question. Restrict attention to fixed target signed graphs $\hat H$ that are irreflexive, bipartite, contain at least one bicoloured edge, and whose s-core has at most two edges. Provide a complete classification: characterise exactly those such $\hat H$ for which List-S-Hom($\hat H$) is solvable in polynomial time, and show that for all remaining such $\hat H$ the problem is NP-complete.
artifact.category_tag: List homomorphism dichotomies for signed graphs
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (Bok, Brewster, Feder, Hell, Jedličková and collaborators, 2022–2024) has confirmed a structural Kim–Siggers-type dichotomy for weakly balanced reflexive and irreflexive signed graphs and established dichotomies for separable signed graphs and signed trees. However, a complete polynomial-vs-NP-complete classification covering all irreflexive bipartite signed targets with a bicoloured edge does not yet appear to be fully established in the literature; partial classifications and conjectures cover important subclasses, so the question seems only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Min Orderings and List Homomorphism Dichotomies for Graphs and Signed Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: We confirm [Kim–Siggers'] conjecture for reflexive and irreflexive signed graphs ... The irreflexive results are new.
status_evidence.claim: A structural dichotomy is established for weakly balanced irreflexive signed graphs, supporting partial progress on the irreflexive bipartite case.

status_evidence.title: List Homomorphisms to Separable Signed Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Dichotomy for list homomorphisms to separable signed graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Dichotomies are known for the separable subclass, but not for all irreflexive bipartite signed targets with a bicoloured edge.

status_evidence.title: Complexity dichotomies for list homomorphism problems of signed graphs (slides)
status_evidence.snippet: Progress towards a classification or even a conjecture has been slow for the list version on signed graphs.
status_evidence.claim: A general dichotomy for List-S-Hom on irreflexive bipartite signed graphs with bicoloured edges is reported as still being investigated.
